subject.title: fix(mac): opening General Settings crashes in packaged app

question: Should OpenClaw accept a local macOS packaging patch of KeyboardShortcuts resource lookup, or wait for and consume a released upstream fix?
rationale: The correct long-term owner of the dependency’s bundle-resolution behavior is an upstream package-contract decision, and the repository policy disfavors new local dependency patches.

options.title: Consume an upstream release
options.body: Require a KeyboardShortcuts release containing the resource-lookup fix, bump to that version, and keep focused packaging regression coverage.

options.title: Accept a narrowly documented local patch
options.body: Explicitly approve the packaging-local patch only with a version pin, upgrade test, and a removal plan tied to the upstream release.

recommendation.title: Consume an upstream release
recommendation.body: Require a KeyboardShortcuts release containing the resource-lookup fix, bump to that version, and keep focused packaging regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor supplied the diagnosis, packaging proof, and current implementation context; a repository owner should make the final dependency-policy call.
